scope: All9 currently explicit Carmel/Monterey gaps; no guesses and no public changes proposed

baseline_finding.reason: No Carmel-by-the-Sea city-limits served-population denominator or complete city-to-water-system allocation was established. The city utilities page identifies California American Water, and the 2025 Monterey system CCR reports compliance, but its multi-community coverage is not a city-only percentage. A system-wide compliant sample table cannot by itself prove the indicator for every city water-system customer. The accepted county fallback also remains unresolved. The 2025 California Annual Compliance Report and full XLSX were retrieved, replacing the earlier inaccessible-report lead. The workbook is violations-only: its 107 Monterey-coded rows represent 54 distinct systems, not all systems or a served-population denominator. EPA ECHO returned 684 Monterey-coded records, 311 active, but its geography fields are not quality-assured service-area allocations and population is estimated average daily system population; summing all system types can duplicate people. No current, boundary-aligned all-system annual denominator was established. CDC Tracking describes water-use and contaminant-specific measures; these do not establish an all-health-based-violations percentage. Tracking California points to contaminant maps and 2022 ACR context; its explorer required JavaScript and embedded viewer was unavailable through the reader. County public-water-system page was blocked (403); the county health-assessment lead is explicitly 2013, outside recency.
baseline_finding.nearest_data: New 2025 Monterey system CA2710004 CCR at https://ear.waterboards.ca.gov/Home/ViewCCR?PwsID=CA2710004&Year=2025&isCert=false, PDF p.2, states water met state and federal drinking-water requirements in 2025. The web reader opens the report, but evidence capture returned 404; provider https://www.amwater.com/ccr/Monterey.pdf redirects to https://amwater.com/_resources/ccr/CA2710004/2025/monterey_2025.pdf and direct download returned 403. The city utility listing is https://ci.carmel.ca.us/post/utilities. State 2025 ACR dataset https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/drinking_water/certlic/drinkingwater/docs/2026/acr-2025-dataset.xlsx lists a WW record for CA2710004, not a demonstrated MCL/MRDL/TT record, and population 92,450; current EPA system population is 128,928. Neither is a Carmel-only population. The 2025 ACR and extraction files, plus CDC/California Tracking checks, document progress beyond the previous 2024-only gap; they do not supply a valid city or county percentage.

dispositions.high_session_disposition: Retain the documented gap. No new compliant number was established. This round audited scope and prior exclusions; it does not claim a new exhaustive search of every source.
dispositions.required_next_evidence: A full annual health-based violation numerator must be joined to a deduplicated, same-period community-system service-population denominator and a defensible population allocation to the city/county. Principal county, counties-served labels and current ECHO HealthFlag alone do not supply that allocation. For Carmel, establish complete city coverage by the relevant system before deriving a city percentage.

baseline_finding.reason: No compliant 2021–2026 median energy burden for low-income households in Carmel-by-the-Sea city limits or the accepted Monterey County fallback was found in this pass. Tier 1 searches of City housing/energy-conservation materials and county sustainability/planning publications found programs/policies rather than the required statistic. The current city Housing page was read, but its Appendix G link and older full 2024 PDF could not be fetched by the web reader. DOE LEAD is unsuitable for the configured median: its December 2024 methodology section 2.3 assigns PUMA housing-type weighted-average income and energy expenditures to tract housing cohorts; DOE FAQ explicitly defines burden using average annual costs divided by average income. Computing a median across those cohort averages would not recover a household median. The 2020 PUMA catalog also shows 0605303 combines southern/eastern Monterey with San Benito County, so a simple union of Monterey-related public-use microdata areas is not full Monterey County alone. No defensible household-level median derivation was identified. Tier 2 DOE/CPUC/Census and Tier 3 ACEEE methods and geography checks therefore did not close the gap. This records a research result, not a claim that the statistic cannot exist.
baseline_finding.nearest_data: New official nearest county context: CPUC CHANGES 2022–2024 Evaluation, dated December 19, 2025, Table 4-18, printed p.70/PDF p.76, lists Monterey average energy burden 2.2% (https://www.cpuc.ca.gov/-/media/cpuc-website/divisions/news-and-outreach/reports/cab/changes/changes-evaluation-report_final.pdf). Section 4.5.3 uses DOE tract averages; this is not a median of low-income households and the table is framed by IOU service territories/limited-English households. Do not score 2.2%. ACEEE September 2024 Data Update Appendix B is an actual median series using 2021 AHS (2019 for starred metros), but no Carmel, Monterey County or Salinas row is present; San Jose 8.5% and San Francisco 7.6% low-income medians are different metro geographies, rejected (https://www.aceee.org/sites/default/files/pdfs/data_update_-_city_energy_burdens_0.pdf). DOE methodology: https://www.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2024-12/lead-methodology_122024.pdf; FAQ: https://www.energy.gov/cmei/scep/slsc/low-income-energy-affordability-data-lead-tool-frequently-asked-questions. Census geography constraint: https://www2.census.gov/geo/maps/DC2020/PUMA/st06_ca/Catalog_PUMAmaps_st06.pdf. Archived PDFs and visually checked exhibits are in energy evidence-additions; no numerical value or score is accepted.

baseline_finding.reason: No city-limits or defensible Monterey County fallback nitrate-groundwater concentration in mg/L NO3-N from the last five years was established in this pass. Recent nearby and agricultural monitoring exists, but the inspected sources do not supply a representative statistic for either accepted jurisdiction. A service-area drinking-water value, subbasin distribution, cumulative exceedance count, or risk index would change the configured indicator or geography.
baseline_finding.nearest_data: City government searches did not retrieve an in-boundary groundwater concentration. MPWMD 2023–2024 Mitigation Program Report, section IV-B, printed pp.IV-2–IV-4 (PDF pp.43–45), monitors the Carmel Valley alluvial aquifer and coastal Seaside Basin; five lower-Carmel-Valley wells were sampled in November 2024, and its published summary emphasizes conductivity/chloride. These networks are not the incorporated city (https://www.mpwmd.net/wp-content/uploads/MPWMD-MitigationReport-finalRY2024.pdf). For the accepted county fallback, Current local-government monitoring was examined before state sources. Monterey Subbasin WY2025 report, section 4.4.3.2 (printed p.87 / PDF p.95), reports selected coastal-well nitrate results from non-detect to approximately 6 mg/L as N, including approximately 5 mg/L in MCWD-30; these are selected wells, not a county statistic (https://www.mcwd.org/docs/gsa/3-004.10_WY_2025.pdf). The Water Board 2025 agricultural memo Figure 2 has 2024 NO3-N distributions and sample counts by subbasin, including East Side, Forebay, Upper Valley and 180/400 Foot; these on-farm domestic wells do not cover all county groundwater (https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/centralcoast/water_issues/programs/ilp/docs/2025/gw-quality-tech-memo.pdf). The 2024 GAP report Tables 2–3 reports 253 Monterey wells tested and 141 nitrate-MCL exceedances over October 2018–July 2024; this voluntary cumulative sample is neither a recent concentration nor representative county coverage (https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/centralcoast/board_info/agendas/2024/dec/item12_stfrpt.pdf). The 2024 Aquifer Risk Map layer uses depth-filtered/de-clustered well data but exposes a 20-year comparison-concentration index, recent exceedance counts and risk classes, not a recent county concentration (https://gispublic.waterboards.ca.gov/portalserver/rest/services/Hosted/Water_Quality_Risk_2024_ARM/FeatureServer/5). County monitoring manual access failed with HTTP 403 in web and evidence capture (https://www.countyofmonterey.gov/home/showpublisheddocument/135929/638648527079730000).

baseline_finding.reason: No defensible 2021-or-newer residential gallons per capita per day observation for Carmel-by-the-Sea city limits, or complete Monterey County fallback, was established in the sources inspected. New MPWMD political-jurisdiction consumption tables are closer than the previous search, but report mixed selected-year averages including 2018-2020 or an unspecified five-year average, with customer accounts rather than a matching resident denominator. Wider utility R-GPCD cannot be assigned to the city. The configured 55 GPCD target is unchanged; no score calculated.
baseline_finding.nearest_data: MPWMD December 4, 2025 Water Demand Committee packet, PDF pages 10-12: Carmel residential consumption 390 AF in the selected-year average (2024, 2021, 2020, 2019, 2018), 2,993 residential customers; a second table gives 390 AF and 3,019 customers for an unspecified five-year average. These tables do not establish a current annual city R-GPCD. https://www.mpwmd.net/wp-content/uploads/Dec-4-2025-WDC-Mtg-Agenda.pdf. City conservation page still links 2011 plan/2012 update (https://ci.carmel.ca.us/post/water-conservation), stale for this indicator. State Water Board per-supplier monthly CSV, directly downloaded and inspected, contains six suppliers labeled Monterey County (878 reports) through August 2026; CalAm Monterey District August 2026 R-GPCD is 67.334788397407 for a reported service population of 96,866. This is a district observation, not a Carmel city or whole-county observation. No verified complete county coverage/crosswalk including small suppliers and self-supplied households was established, so supplier rates were not averaged or divided by total county population. Raw CSV and reproducible coverage extraction: calculations/freshwater-withdrawals/inspect.py and coverage-inspection.json. Dataset URL: https://publish.data.ca.gov/dataset/c69ac02b-adfb-459a-bc58-bf69a8b572d2/resource/f4d50112-5fb5-4066-b45c-44696b10a49e/download/monthly_combined_dataset.csv. USGS current guide (https://www.usgs.gov/mission-areas/water-resources/science/accessing-water-use-data/) identifies latest modeled public-supply estimates through 2020 and historic county compilations through 2015, outside the five-year rule; public supply also includes nonresidential demand.

baseline_finding.reason: No 2021-or-newer whole-county or permitted regional community GHG inventory was verified in this pass. The adopted June 2026 AMBAG 2050 MTP/SCS Final EIR identifies 2019/2020 as its most-current regional inventory. Its nominal 2022 baseline interpolates every non-road source between 2020 and forecast 2025, so its recent label cannot establish a recent observed community inventory. County CCAAP inventories cover unincorporated areas and cannot stand for all Monterey County.
baseline_finding.nearest_data: New evidence: AMBAG May 2026 Final EIR, adopted June 10, 2026: https://www.ambag.org/sites/default/files/2026-05/AMBAG_2050%20MTPSCS_FEIR_Combined%20May%202026_Acc.pdf. Table 4.8-1 (PDF pp348–349) reports a 2019/2020 tri-county inventory; methodology at printed 4.8-21 and Table 4.8-2 footnote 1 (PDF p368, printed 4.8-23) explains that 2022 non-road emissions are interpolated from the 2045 MTP/SCS forecast using 2020 and 2025. Regional boundary is Monterey, San Benito and Santa Cruz counties; do not attribute its mean to Monterey County. AMBAG FY2022–23 audited report documents 2020 community inventories for 3CE jurisdictions: https://www.ambag.org/sites/default/files/2024-02/Official%20-%20FINAL%2022_23%20ACFR_1_25_24_0.pdf (p17). 3CE membership omits King City, and 2020 is outside the recency window. Updated County CCAAP still uses 2019 unincorporated emissions: https://monterey.legistar.com/LegislationDetail.aspx?FullText=1&GUID=F6F00ECF-57EF-4163-B7E1-81DC2FAD2479&ID=8013107. CARB current inventory is statewide (https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/ghg-inventory-data); EPA PCAP inventory directory has no Salinas/Monterey entry (https://www.epa.gov/inflation-reduction-act/ghg-inventories-searchable-table). Climate TRACE has recent territorial source emissions, but this pass did not establish a matching community accounting boundary including imported electricity and community waste; its sum was not substituted for community inventory (https://climatetrace.org/data; https://climatetrace.org/news/clearing-the-path-to-easier-more-accurate-scope-3-emissions). No denominator or extrapolated value was fabricated.
